title: Paris in Hysteria
subtitle: No remedy exists to cure this mania—not even the warmth of a dreamy summer afternoon.

trails.title: Who's there?
trails.description: Theivery is a craft that demands both courage and skill. But above all, luck.

content.text:
"Are we seriously waiting all night? I'm not sure this is worth it."
"Trust me, Paul. This is our big chance. I saw him go in right here."
"The Catacombs? It's just a pile of bones. Everyone in Paris knows that."
"He had suitcases. Heavy ones. I bet he's hiding something big. It's all ours when he leaves."
"Did you hear that?"
"Shh! He's coming out!"
"Wait ... was the guy you saw ... this massive?"
"No way ... look at his head. No, wait, what's wrong with his hands?"
"He's coming this way ... Did he see us? He saw us!"
"Run, Paul! Come on! Go, go, go!"
Chants from marches and protests echo through the streets. You begin thinking about the roots of this era's unrest. Those surges of fear, anxiety, and anger—perhaps they come from:
The collapse of morals and the decay of the human heart.

branch.text: Vile people with no sense of virtue.

content.text: A crisis of civilization and primal aggression.
A breakdown of connection and distance between people.

branch.text: No one truly understands anyone else.

content.text: A world out of order and a universe out of balance.

branch.text: Maybe the gods have lost their minds.

items.text: Adèle forces a broken smile to her face.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame Bouanich, as much as I appreciate your humor, now really isn't the time for it. Where did she go?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I'm quite used to her attitude, but stealing that necklace crosses a line!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Adèle.
The distance in her voice and manners disappears—the diviner becomes mortal. Her voice laced with genuine concern.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Félicienne was never here.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Perhaps it fell out of your pocket. Allow me to aid you in its return. I believe it is best you not act alone in your current state.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah, I've got it now. She didn't come to your parlor today, so she must've gone somewhere else, and she's been waiting in the car ever since. No wonder she got angry and stormed off.
She fidgets with her sleeve button, desperate to escape this farce.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ay ay ay, that's enough! What a day! I think it's better we speak again another time, Madame Bouanich. Would tomorrow work? I—

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: When did you first meet this Félicienne?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Oh, my goodness!
Beryl moves faster, forcing the car door closed.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Honestly, what on earth is happening today?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You want proof? I'll give you proof. Hah, madness! Never thought I'd have to actually convince someone that I work for that terrible woman.
She rummages impatiently through her pockets until she finds her wallet.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It was raining. She started complaining about the mud on her shoes the moment she stepped into the car, then insisted we head straight to the Champs-Élysées.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You know, wealthy young ladies like her are always generous with payment. I often have to take time out of my evenings just to count all her tips. That very first day, she even gave me some gold francs as keepsakes. I've got them in here.
Her face twists in disbelief as she flips it open and closes it again.
Not a single coin or bill.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Oh. Hah. I must've put them somewhere else.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Give me a moment to check the car. I've got other proof, too!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah. The macaron boxes. There's a full one somewhere! And her hair, little bits and pieces she left in the car.
For a brief moment, she accepts the absurd conclusion.
Félicienne never existed.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I remember ... that day ...
Her every recollection of Félicienne takes on a strange blur, as if she were viewing them from behind a fogged-up windshield.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I ... I must be tired. It's been a long day. It'll come to me soon.
Beryl strokes the back of her hand, gently urging her to let go of the empty wallet.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: But there is nothing to remember.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Something's wrong with me. Prophecies, dreams, the necklace—it's all playing havoc with my mind.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I need to clear my head! Just bear with me. Those coins have to be in here somewhere.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Do not worry, Adèle. It is not only you who is confused in this era.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Look at the people around you.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: People?
Sound crashes back in. She rubs her temples, fighting the dizziness.

items.speaker: Protester I
items.text: No more atrocities! No more oppression!

items.speaker: Protester II
items.text: Liberty! Equality!

items.speaker: Protester III
items.text: Stand with Paris! Stand with the people!

items.speaker: Protester IV
items.text: For the commune! For France!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Excuse me, sir.
Beryl calls out to the nearest worker—a man waving a bright red Phrygian cap.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Where are you going?

items.speaker: Protester I
items.text: We're following the Garde Nationale to fight the royalists!

items.speaker: Protester II
items.text: Yes, and then I'm going straight to the pawnbroker to get my mattress back!

items.speaker: Protester I
items.text: You do that, sister! Brighter days lie just ahead if we fight as one for our city!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It is no easy feat. But your voices today may echo further than you know. You will triumph in time.

items.speaker: Protester I
items.text: Thank you, madame! For the Commune de Paris!
The man turns and disappears into the crowd.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Well, everyone's fighting to survive these days. Looks like another protest.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But did he just say "Commune de Paris"?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: He did. In their minds, this is the burning summer of 1871.
Those almost-transparent eyes again. People's thoughts pass through her like light through crystal. Beryl reads them but never bends to them.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Unconscious thoughts, countless in number, are converging upon this city. This is a volatile time indeed.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Some worry for their missing family and friends, some are terrified by ghosts and spirits, some obsess over a long-dead emperor, and others are shaken by the phantom attacks of a beast of legend.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The edifice of reality is shaking. Chaos has been invited into its foundation.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Whispered fears, murmured madnesses ... A sickness is sweeping the city, and the Beasts of Gévaudan have multiplied.
She watches the flow of the moving crowd.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Those who invited this chaos did not comprehend that the flaws of reality are not the fault of a single person nor group of people. This is not the way to mend Paris.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Everyone—everything—has an identity, whether it be individual or collective. To attempt to unify them all so recklessly will not create order, but chaos.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Chaos is what turned those people into beasts.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You mean the sightings of the Beasts of Gévaudan were all people? That the citizens of Paris have been turning into monsters?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Then are they the ones who killed Madame Raymond? Who cursed me, took Célia, and trapped all these protesters in this delusion?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: And Félicienne, too?
The things she describes are fairy tales, myths, urban legends meant to scare children. They aren't real. They aren't meant to be believed.
She grits her teeth, unable to reconcile her doubts with her experiences.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Truthfully, madame, I'm having a hard time believing you or even my own eyes.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Everything turned completely mad the moment I entered your parlor.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The Beasts of Gévaudan were nothing more than a rumor before I met you, but in your parlor—in that dream—there they were, attacking me!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: And now you claim that Félicienne isn't real, that I just made her up! What are you trying to do here?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I play no part in your fate, Adèle. It is what brought you here. I am only a witness.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: "Only a witness"! You've got a clever answer for everything, don't you? Then tell me where the necklace is. You must've seen Félicienne take it, right?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So? Did you "witness" that, madame?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You received that necklace in a dream.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It is only natural that it would vanish into another.
Her reasoning is as solid as it is absurd.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: That necklace proves the truth of my words. The spirit world is as real to us as the physical world.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I will happily read Félicienne's fate. That is, if you still believe she is real.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I don't need you to read anything!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I-I need space! To get away from all this madness and think for myself!
Beryl steps back from the car door, unconsciously giving way, allowing Adèle to lunge forward and seize the handle.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Adèle ...
The ringing in her ears returns, and the street noise rushes in all at once.
But she's made up her mind. If she can just get in, start the engine ...

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Adèle! Behind you!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Wha—
A damp, metallic breath brushes her neck.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Stay close to me.
Adèle reacts instantly, pulling back with Beryl's tug, raising her arm.
A burst of flame shoots from her fingertips. Her little dragon beats its wings, setting the beast ablaze before it can fade away.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Your hand! Did it get you?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Bloody hell! This is no dream! How did they get here?
Shouts rise from the nearby crowd.
Adèle gasps, scanning the street. Seeing no second monster, she finally exhales.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Is that what you meant earlier?
The diviner nods faintly, blood running down her now-paler skin.
If they'd been a moment slower, Beryl's arm wouldn't be the only one bleeding. Adèle doesn't believe she's worth that kind of sacrifice.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Maybe you do have a point. At least about the Beasts of Gévaudan.
She opens the car door, searching inside with purpose, before handing Beryl a handkerchief.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Here, take this. It should help with the bleeding. *sigh* I can't just leave you like this. You'll have to come with me, madame.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But I'm afraid I can't take you home. I must find my friends before anything happens to them.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I can't just leave them wandering the city while these monsters prowl the streets.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Is that so?
She looks surprised but accepts the gesture.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I foresaw death in the catacombs, and yet still you aim to go there.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Of course.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I've made up my mind. I need to find Célia. I don't care what it costs.
Adèle pauses, her vision locked on Beryl's bleeding arm.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I'm still not sure if I can trust you. But for now, at least, I don't believe you want to do me any harm.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But I need to know—why are you helping me?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You didn't even ask for payment. What do you want from me?

Beryl's translucent eyes barely restrain a visible roll. It's affectionate—almost motherly.
Her question is harmless, if utterly naive.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: So this is what you choose to ask.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Why wouldn't it be?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Of all there is to question—your future, this chaos—you choose to ask about me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What's so strange about that?
Her flawless, gentle smile returns, from matron back to diviner.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Nothing. Your curiosity is only natural.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I have never once lied to you, Adèle. You are cursed—haunted by a shadow. A shadow of fate.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I only wish to see what will become of you.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But don't you already know? I'll die in the catacombs. What else is there to see?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You know this yourself. Yet here we are.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: We have a common interest in that fate, you and I. Let us leave it at that.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Go to the catacombs, Adèle, with me by your side. You will need my help once you enter.
It's a long-delayed request to travel together.
Adèle can't read much from Beryl's expression, but there's no time left.
After a brief thought, she opens the car door again.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Please, get in. Careful. Let me open the door.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Thank you.
The Peugeot 201 slips through the crowd, turning down a quiet street toward its destined end.
